text.p: An easing U.S. dollar and widespread insecurity about the U.S. and European interest rate developments soured sentiment in the Swiss share market, leading to a close below the 4,600 point level on the blue-chip index.
Volume was below that of the past few sessions and trade was influenced by derivative transactions, share traders said.
The blue-chip SMI index fell 79.7 points, or 1.72 percent, to 4,556.5 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 42.02 points, or 1.43 percent, to 2,891.84.
"I think the recent rally is pretty much over," one trader said. "A level above 4,700 points was probably clearly exaggerated," he added in a reference to the March 11 all-time high of 4,734.1.
Ciba Specialty Chemicals led the actives list. After initially holding up against the weaker market trend, the shares closed with a slump of 5.25 francs, or 4.18 percent, at 120.25.
Novartis registered shares fell 18 francs to 1,739. The company is due to release its 1996 results on Tuesday. Roche certificates fell 245 francs to 12,190.

Inspection and testing group Surveillance fell 150 francs to 3,280. The firm reported a 14 percent 1996 profit increase to 262.7 million francs compared to 230.4 million in 1995. It also increased its dividend.
Banks were among the major losers of the day. UBS slid 29 francs, or 2.17 percent, to 1,307. CS Group was down 4.75 francs to 163,50.
Industrials Sulzer and Holderbank bucked the trend. Sulzer, which is expected to report on its outlook on Tuesday, rose two francs to 979. The company has already released its 1996 results.
